```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2)
```

`beatpool` pools patient-specific principal component bases of ECG heartbeats
without sharing the raw signals. Each site sends a small summary, either a
`p x q` basis or a set of leading eigenpairs, and the server assembles a common
representation. This vignette walks through the main functions on simulated
data that mimic the heterogeneity of real recordings.

## Simulating heterogeneous records

```{r simulate}
library(beatpool)

sim <- simulate_beats(H = 8, n = 200, p = 61, q = 10,
                      model = "heterogeneous", epsilon = 0.2,
                      sigma = 0.15, seed = 1)
str(sim$X[[1]])
```

The records share a common eigenbasis `Q0` but each one is rotated by an
orthogonal matrix. The rotation is the source of the federation problem: the
individual bases are not comparable entry by entry.

## Patient bases

```{r bases}
bases <- extract_bases(sim$X, q = 10)
bases[[1]]
round(crossprod(bases[[1]]$T), 3)[1:4, 1:4]
```

`extract_bases()` returns one `bp_basis` object per record. The columns are
orthonormal, but their signs, order and orientation are arbitrary.

## Pooling

Four pooling operators are available. The orthogonal Procrustes mean is the
default and minimises the average squared Frobenius distance to the inputs.

```{r pool}
p_proc <- pool_bases(bases, method = "procrustes")
p_bar  <- pool_bases(bases, method = "bar")
p_qr   <- pool_bases(bases, method = "qr")
p_proc
```

Pooling second moments is an alternative that requires no alignment at all.
The assembled covariance

$$
\hat\Sigma = \sum_h w_h Q_h \Lambda_h Q_h'
$$

is invariant to any orthogonal transformation of $Q_h$, because the outer
product absorbs it.

```{r spectral}
p_spec <- pool_spectral(bases, q = 10, q_out = 10)
p_cov  <- pool_covariance(sim$X, q = 10)
p_spec
```

## Comparing every operator

`pool_all()` runs the operator families on the same bases and records the
communication cost of each one. The spectral summary transmits `q * (p + 1)`
numbers, the basis operators `p * q`, and the covariance `p * (p + 1) / 2`.

```{r all}
all <- pool_all(sim$X, q = 10)
attr(all, "numbers")
```

The cost--error plane can be drawn directly from the collection.

```{r cost-error, fig.height = 4}
err <- vapply(all, function(T) mean(vapply(sim$X, reconstruction_error,
  numeric(1), T = T, k = 3)), numeric(1))
plot_cost_error(all, err, k = 3)
```

## Reconstruction on held-out beats

```{r reconstruction}
X_new <- simulate_beats(H = 1, n = 200, p = 61, q = 10,
                        model = "heterogeneous", epsilon = 0.2,
                        sigma = 0.15, seed = 99)$X[[1]]

ks <- 1:10
err <- data.frame(
  k = ks,
  procrustes = vapply(ks, function(k)
    reconstruction_error(X_new, p_proc$T, k), numeric(1)),
  spectral = vapply(ks, function(k)
    reconstruction_error(X_new, p_spec$T, k), numeric(1)),
  covariance = vapply(ks, function(k)
    reconstruction_error(X_new, p_cov$T, k), numeric(1)),
  local = vapply(ks, function(k)
    reconstruction_error(X_new, bases[[1]]$T, k), numeric(1))
)

matplot(err$k, err[, -1], type = "b", pch = 1:4, lty = 1,
        xlab = "components", ylab = "relative reconstruction error")
legend("topright", names(err)[-1], pch = 1:4, lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

The local basis is an oracle: it is fitted on the same recording. The pooled
bases should approach it as the number of records grows.

## Downstream clustering

```{r clustering}
mix <- simulate_beats(H = 1, n = 400, p = 61, q = 10, model = "mixture",
                      mu = 1.5, sigma = 0.2, seed = 2)
X <- mix$X[[1]]
cl <- cluster_beats(X, p_proc$T, k = 5, K = 2, truth = mix$labels[[1]],
                    seed = 1)
cl$metrics
```

## Rate and distortion

The pooled operator is meant to be transmitted, so the basis is only useful if
its coefficients can be stored in few bits. `rate_distortion()` quantises each
coefficient with a uniform scalar quantiser, entropy-codes the integer levels
and charges the basis and the mean once per record, amortised over its beats.

```{r ratedistortion}
rd <- rate_distortion(X_new, p_spec$T, k = 10,
                      steps = 2^seq(0, -6, by = -1))
rd[, c("step", "rate", "distortion", "compression_ratio")]
plot(rd$rate, rd$distortion, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "bits per beat", ylab = "mean relative error (%)")
```

The compression ratio is taken against the raw signal at 11 bits per sample.
Pass `transmit_basis = FALSE` for a fixed transform such as the DCT, which the
decoder already knows, and `n_amortize` to change the number of beats over
which the basis is amortised.

## Reading WFDB files

The package contains a pure-R reader for MIT-BIH style records, so the whole
pipeline can run without external WFDB software.

```{r wfdb, eval = FALSE}
x <- read_wfdb("100", dir = "data/mitdb")
ann <- read_annotations("data/mitdb/atr/100.atr")
X <- prepare_record(x$MLII, ann, record = "100", fs = 360, wsize = 30)
b <- pca_basis(X, q = 10)
```

## Stability

Jackknife stability measures how much the pooled basis changes when one
recording is removed.

```{r stability}
loo <- leave_one_out_pool(bases)
jackknife_stability(loo)
```

## Several shared bases

When records differ, a single basis leaves structure unused. Each record can
transmit the eigenpairs of its energy-normalised moment, and the receiver can
group them into a few shared bases without asking the records for anything else.
A record then compresses with the basis of lowest error and sends its index.

```{r shared}
sim <- simulate_beats(H = 12, n = 100, p = 30, q = 3, epsilon = 0.5, seed = 7)
moments <- lapply(sim$X, energy_moment, q = 6)
fit <- pool_shared(moments, k = 3, C = 3, seed = 1)
fit
select_shared(fit, sim$X[[1]])
```
